442:
We'll return your charges
to prison today.
443:
What if you find the coat-check attendant?
Might you need us again?
444:
I didn't want to tell you this,
but Bely—Docent—escaped today.
445:
Hard to believe, but true.
It's dangerous for you to keep up this disguise.
446:
Could we wait until tomorrow?
It's New Year, and they tried in their own way.
447:
We're staying out of town.
Docent is unlikely to find us.
448:
All right, but don't leave the house!
And we forwarded your letter
449:
to Sheremetyev's wife.
Here's her reply, addressed to him.
450:
- You'll have lunch with us on the first. Promise?
- We promise!
451:
What a shame. She's such a nice woman,
but her father's a fence and a profiteer.
452:
What's all this shouting? Who said you could go out?
- You're back... Bad person.
454:
The New Year is here.
I hope it brings each of you a new life.
455:
Anything can happen, but know this:
wherever you are, wherever I am,
456:
I'll always remember you.
I'll be sure to find you.
457:
- And now... Just a moment.
- Where's he going?
458:
Who knows?
You can't make sense of him anymore.
459:
What's to make sense of?
He says he'll find us anywhere and cut our throats.
461:
They say he went straight across Ryaboy's throat
with a razor. That was that. - He's turned into a savage.
462:
Who's come to see you?
Father Frost, with presents for you!
463:
- Come here, Fedya. - What did I do?
- Come on. Wear these at home.
464:
- What do I need them for? I don't even have a home.
- You will. It's all ahead of you.
465:
- They'll come in handy in prison for now. Wear them.
- Always predicting the worst.
466:
This is for you, Vasya.
And this is for you, Gavrila Petrovich. - Thank you.
467:
- Pure wool.
- This is for you too.
469:
Sour stuff.
It's dull without vodka.
470:
- Must you drink yourself senseless?
- What else can we do?
471: We could sit and have a heart-to-heart.
472:
I'm not a prosecutor. I don't do
heart-to-hearts. - We could play a game.
473:
Listen to him! Think I'm a sucker
who'd play cards with you? You've got nine aces in your deck.
474: It doesn't have to be cards.
475:
Here's a good game: cities.
I say "Moscow,"
476:
and you name one beginning with W: Warsaw.
Then you name one beginning with W. Understand?
477:
Your turn, Fedya.
Name a city beginning with W.
478:
Vorkuta.
Why? I did time there.
479:
- All right. Your turn, beginning with A.
- Dzhambul. - What's Dzhambul got to do with it?
480:
It's warm there. It's my home.
My mother lives there.
481:
Let's play something else. I'll go out,
you hide something, and I'll come back and find it.
482:
- You'd do better finding the helmet.
- Be quiet.
483:
- We'll hide it, but he'll peep through a hole!
- Then you go out and hide it.
484:
You watch to make sure I don't peep.
- Why me? It's always Fedya when something needs doing.
485:
- I'll rip your mouth off, you little scoundrel!
- My mouth, my mouth...
486:
- Docent, were you ever little?
- Yes.
487:
- Did you have a mother and father?
- Yes.
488:
Why are you so mean?
Why do you act like a dog?
490:
- He came to me himself.
- So you're here too.
491:
I tried your place,
but I could tell it was being watched.
492: Mityai, I need somewhere to hide.
494:
- Where are we going?
- Keep walking.
495:
- Sorry to trouble you for nothing, Doctor.
- It's all right.
496:
Give him valerian, some warm tea,
and let him sleep. - Thank you.
497:
- Does it hurt, Garik?
- It hurts, Vasya. Read it.
499:
"Dear Dad, hello! We found out
you're in prison
500:
and were very happy,
because we thought you were dead."
501:
What bastard told his kid
about Sourpuss?
502:
"Mom was happy too. When your letter came,
she cried all day,
503:
though she'd told me
you were a test pilot."
505:
"I'm glad you're alive anyway,
because Mom says
506:
you're a good man,
just weak-willed."
507:
That's right! Weak-willed enough
to steal our money and blame the taxi driver.
508:
Scram! I'll knock your horns off,
you rat!
510:
Shame on you! You're forty years old.
Half your lives are already over.
511:
What's behind you? What do you have now?
What lies ahead?
512:
Darkness, filth, and nothing human!
Come to your senses before it's too late. That's my advice.
513:
Docent, we need to get out of here.
That doctor will tell the police.
514:
- She won't. - Why not?
- I took a razor to her throat.
515:
She's in the well.
Go look if you like.
516: What was my sentence? One year.
518:
For the kindergarten and the apartment?
Let's say ten!
519:
- How much is that altogether?
- Fourteen.
520:
And I'm supposed to put up with that snake
for a lousy fourteen years?
521:
The one who put the old woman in the well?
Do what you want. I'm going to the police.
522: Go on! He won't touch you.
523:
And you two? You'll put up with him
till the day you die?
524:
Vasya, I told him I had a cold earlier,
and he...
525:
Enough about your cold!
Come here...
527:
- What are you doing?
- Cleaning the rug.
528:
Listen, comrades. The show's over.
First, I'll take this off.
530:
I'll serve out my sentence, and that's it.
I'm going straight! I'll get a job.
531:
- Doing what?
- Watchman at the collective farm back home.
- Why watchman?
532:
I could clear snow, lay bricks,
or be an interpreter. I know English.
533:
If only we'd brought the hat!
What's Docent? A crook.
534:
- There are plenty of crooks, but only one hat.
- They'd shorten our sentences for that helmet.
535:
Where did he put it?
We've checked everywhere.
536:
Crook! I told you I had a cold,
and all you said was, "Your mouth, your mouth."
537:
- You made me dive in freezing weather!
- When did he make you dive?
538:
When they caught us. Remember?
He said he'd fish, and I should dive.
539:
- Wait. What did he say about fishing?
- "I'm fishing through a hole in the ice,"
540:
- then he asked if I could swim.
- He hid the helmet in that ice hole!
541:
That's right! I remember, the bad person!
It's in the ice hole at Malakhovka!
542:
Why didn't you say so, you lout?
You could've left a note before hanging yourself. - Let's go.
543:
- What about him?
- They can collect him. I'm not carrying that great lump. Come on!
545:
- There's nothing there.
- It's there, at the bottom. Someone has to dive.
546:
Why me? It's always Cross-Eye!
Vasya, tell him to do it himself.
547: I can't! It's cold. I'll get sick.
548:
- You tried to hang yourself, and now you're afraid of a cold?
- Sporting greetings!
550:
- Where's the boat station?
- Over there.
551:
I'd kill you all
if I had the time!
552:
Now there are two of him.
And there's another at the country house.
554:
- One!
- Well done, Fyodor Petrovich! Well done!
555:
- Two.
- The more we turn in, the better.
